standard_prerequisites.name: For a quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal the derived category of quasi-coherent modules agrees with the full derived category of quasi-coherent sheaves
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof replace one category by the other and compare the two functors on the same objects.

standard_prerequisites.name: A pushforward along an affine morphism whose source category has an exact left adjoint preserves K-injective complexes, so it can be used to compute derived pushforwards
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that pushing forward a K-injective complex of quasi-coherent modules from an affine open is again K-injective and represents its derived pushforward.

standard_prerequisites.name: The pushforward along an affine morphism of a quasi-coherent complex represents its derived pushforward
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the values of both functors on the complexes coming from an affine open.

core_obligations: Identify the two categories by the equivalence available for quasi-compact schemes with affine diagonal, so that the statement becomes the claim that the canonical map from the right derived functor to the derived pushforward is an isomorphism on all objects (proof lines 1842-1850).
Record the two out of three property: if the statement holds for two objects of a distinguished triangle, then it holds for the third (proof lines 1851-1855).

For an affine open of the source, note that the inclusion and the composed morphism to the base are affine, and use that the pushforward along the inclusion has an exact left adjoint to conclude that it preserves K-injective complexes (proof lines 1856-1862).

Compute both functors on a complex pushed forward from that affine open: the first is the pushforward along the composed affine morphism, the second the same by the identification of pushforwards along affine morphisms with derived pushforwards, and the composition of derived pushforwards gives the equality (proof lines 1863-1870).

Use the two out of three property, together with generators of the derived category obtained by pushing forward from affine opens, to extend the statement from the complexes of that form to all objects, which concludes the proof (proof lines 1871-1911).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to comparing the two functors on the common category and record the two out of three property (proof lines 1842-1855).
Check the statement on complexes pushed forward from an affine open using K-injective representatives (proof lines 1856-1870).
Extend to all objects by generating the category from such complexes (proof lines 1871-1911).
